name: Player empowerment
scopeNote: Player empowerment / man-management football: light prescriptive structure, rules on discipline and defending without the ball, freedom with the ball, authority built through relationships. Exemplars: Ancelotti (Real Madrid 2021-25, also 2013-15), Zidane (Real Madrid 2016-18 and 2019-21), Scaloni (Argentina 2018-ongoing). Sources use 'man-management', 'freedom' and 'social competence'; the label 'anti-tactician' is contested (Sky Sports argues freedom is itself a tactic). Exact appointment and exit dates were not verified in mined pages; 2016-01-04 (Zidane appointment) is from memory and the period is the union of exemplar eras. Argentina with Scaloni is covered mainly by FIFA's Coaches Forum; formation labels vary widely between sources.
openQuestions: Proposed manager ids: zinedine-zidane and lionel-scaloni do not exist in research/manager; only carlo-ancelotti does. Create or rename.
Exemplar team ids not checked/assigned (e.g. Real Madrid 2021-25, Argentina 2022); none proposed to avoid inventing ids.

Zidane is described as 'chaotic' and lucky in FourFourTwo while a rotation-based man-manager; Scaloni is more structurally explicit (three-to-five second counter-press, system changes), so the 'light structure' label fits Ancelotti best.
Ancelotti is quoted in a 2022 press conference saying the defensive side 'is very important'; empowerment applies to the ball, not to defending.
No source found on zonal vs man-marking for Zidane or Scaloni; Ancelotti zonal claims came only from search summaries (UEFA page not accessible).
Exact dates of spells to confirm: Zidane 2016-01-04 to 2018-05-31 and 2019-03-11 to 2021-05-27; Ancelotti 2021-06-01 to 2025-05; Scaloni interim 2018-09, permanent 2019.

statedView.quote: If Vinicius or Rodrygo feel more comfortable opening up a little more on the wings when the team has the ball, I am not going to tell them to stay inside, because it is an individual interpretation of the game.
I give the players plenty of freedom. The video sessions don’t last more than fifteen minutes. They have fun together, and there’s a great atmosphere among them.

It’s the most important thing for a manager, the relationship he has with the players. You can talk all you want about tactics or techniques, but if you don’t have the players on your side, you won’t have the collective motivation to put a system in place or the players to make it work.
